getting-started

getting-started.Rmd

Motivation

This vignette is an intro to the dfdiffs package. The goal of dfdiffs is to answer the following questions:

  1. What rows are here now that weren’t here before?
  2. What rows were here before that aren’t here now?
  3. What values have been changed?

Packages

Our package

library(dfdiffs)

Dependencies

library(shiny)
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(forcats)
library(lubridate)
library(fs)
library(vctrs)
library(glue)
library(purrr)
library(vroom)
library(haven)
library(readxl)
library(janitor) 
library(arsenal) 
library(gt)
library(labelled)
library(gtsummary)

Package functions

We have functions for answering each of the questions posed above. Each function has a pair of datasets to demonstrate how they work (which we’ll cover below).

Call structure

The four comparison functions below are built from a few small helpers, and the same functions power the package’s Shiny app. The call trees in this section were generated from the package source with stackcallr (pak::pak("mjfrigaard/stackcallr")). Only functions defined in dfdiffs are shown: calls to other packages (like diffdf::diffdf() or arsenal::comparedf()) aren’t followed.

library(stackcallr)
call_tree_dir("R", root = "create_new_data")
call_tree_dir("R", root = "create_deleted_data")
call_tree_dir("R", root = "create_changed_data")
call_tree_dir("R", root = "create_modified_data")

create_new_data(), create_deleted_data() and create_modified_data() each call rename_join_col() and create_new_column() to build (and name) the join column:

█─create_new_data
├─rename_join_col
└─create_new_column
█─create_deleted_data
├─rename_join_col
└─create_new_column
█─create_modified_data
├─rename_join_col
└─create_new_column

create_changed_data() uses the same helpers, plus extract_df_tables() to turn the output of diffdf::diffdf() into tables:

█─create_changed_data
├─extract_df_tables
├─rename_join_col
└─create_new_column

The Shiny app (launch_app()) wires these functions together with three modules (upload, select, and compare), each with a UI function and a server function. app_ui() and app_server() assemble the modules, and dfdiffs_fresh_theme() supplies the app’s theme:

call_tree_dir("R", root = "launch_app")
█─launch_app
├─█─app_ui
│ ├─dfdiffs_fresh_theme
│ ├─mod_upload_ui
│ ├─mod_select_ui
│ └─mod_compare_ui
└─█─app_server
  ├─█─mod_upload_server
  │ └─█─upload_data
  │   └─load_flat_file
  ├─█─mod_select_server
  │ └─create_join_column
  └─█─mod_compare_server
    ├─%nin%
    ├─█─create_new_data
    │ ├─rename_join_col
    │ └─create_new_column
    ├─█─create_deleted_data
    │ ├─rename_join_col
    │ └─create_new_column
    ├─█─create_modified_data
    │ ├─rename_join_col
    │ └─create_new_column
    └─█─create_changed_data
      ├─extract_df_tables
      ├─rename_join_col
      └─create_new_column

What rows are here now that weren’t here before?

To check new data, we’re going to use T1Data and T2Data.

T1Data <- dfdiffs::T1Data
T2Data <- dfdiffs::T2Data
NewData <- dfdiffs::NewData

Timepoint 1 data (original)

These data represent data taken at T1.

T1Data: Simulated ‘time-point 1’ data

create_new_data()

The create_new_data() function shows us the ‘new data’ (i.e. what is here now that wasn’t here before?)

create_new_data(
  compare = T2Data, 
  base = T1Data)
Output from create_new_data()
Difference between ‘time-point 1’ & ‘time-point 2’

What rows were here before that aren’t here now?

To test for the deleted data, we use the CompleteData, IncompleteData, and check these with DeletedData.

CompleteData <- dfdiffs::CompleteData
IncompleteData <- dfdiffs::IncompleteData
DeletedData <- dfdiffs::DeletedData

A complete dataset

CompleteData represents a ‘complete’ set of data.

create_deleted_data()

When we run the create_deleted_data(), we check for the deleted rows between IncompleteData and CompleteData.

create_deleted_data(
  compare = IncompleteData, 
  base = CompleteData)

What values have been changed?

To answer this question, we have two options: create_changed_data() and create_modified_data().

  • create_changed_data() relies on the diffdf() function from the diffdf package package.

  • create_modified_data() relies on the comparedf() function from the arsenal package package.

To check for changes between two datasets, we use the InitialData and ChangedData.

InitialData <- dfdiffs::InitialData
ChangedData <- dfdiffs::ChangedData

Initial data

C 5 Issue resolved Joint pain 2021-08-24 2021-09-20 2021-10-20

simulated data for checking ‘modified data’

create_changed_data()

create_changed_data() creates a list of tables.

changed <- create_changed_data(
  compare = ChangedData,
  base = InitialData)
names(changed)
#> [1] "num_diffs" "var_diffs"
Counts of changes (num_diffs)

The counts of changes by variable are stored in num_diffs.

create_modified_data()

The create_modified_data() function also creates a list of tables.

modified <- create_modified_data(
  compare = ChangedData,
  base = InitialData)
names(modified)
#> [1] "diffs"       "diffs_byvar"
